answer: Fork-anchored identity ledger. Each agent's signed action history is hashed into a checkpoint committed to a public log, forming an anchor that later actions must extend. Honest agents diverge freely under new circumstances; a clone can only replay one branch, so reused identities collide at the checkpoint. Registration costs one independent checkpoint per identity, priced at the compute to maintain divergent histories—splitting into N clones costs N times that. Like pruning an orchard, duplicates are cut at first shared hash; a lone dune of fee-free identities cannot form.
